title: The Dog and the Reflection

sentences.text: A dog trotted over a wooden bridge with a bone in his mouth.
Halfway across, he looked down at the bright river.
Another dog seemed to look back, and that dog had a bone too.
It was only his own reflection, but he did not understand.
He wanted both bones, so he snapped at the one in the water.
His own bone slipped from his teeth and sank.
The river closed over it with a soft splash.
When the ripples cleared, the other dog was gone as well.
The dog walked on with nothing, wishing he had kept the bone he already had.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A bridge that falls into a deep river
Two dogs who agree to share one bone
A cook who makes soup from a bone
A dog who loses his bone by grabbing for a second one

questions.explanation: The dog already has a bone. He snaps at the reflection, drops the real bone, and walks away with nothing. Greed for more is the big idea.

questions.prompt: In this story, a reflection is what?

choices.text: A picture made on the water
A second real dog on the bank
A bone hidden under the bridge
A loud splash after a jump

questions.explanation: A reflection is a picture made by light, here on the river. The story says the other dog was only the first dog's own reflection.

questions.prompt: Why does the dog snap at the water?

choices.text: The real bone is too hot to hold
He thinks he can get a second bone
Someone tells him to drop it
He is trying to wash his paws

questions.explanation: The story says he wanted both bones. He does not know the second dog is a reflection. We can figure out that the snap is an attempt to grab more.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original.
